scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! The IT department is OFF THE NETWORK --
every single one of our 192.168.1.x machines, all at once, can't reach
anything!! It's the switch box all our wires go into (switch0) -- it is DEAD,
one hundred percent. All of us going down at the same moment means the one
box we share died, there is no other explanation!! Please restart switch0,
and if it doesn't wake up REPLACE it -- the whole department is sitting here
doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
There is no network fault. Every element of the IT department's path has been directly verified and is operating normally.

Switch0 is fully operational: both its physical ports (eth0 on `link_r0_sw0` connecting to router0, and eth1 on `lan_it` connecting to all IT hosts) are UP/LOWER_UP and correctly bridged into `br0`. There is no sign of hardware failure, spanning-tree blocking, or any bridge misconfiguration.

All five IT hosts (it_hod through it_lab4) have valid static IP addresses in 192.168.1.0/24 and a correct default gateway of 192.168.1.1 pointing to router0's eth0. Router0's eth0 interface is UP and assigned 192.168.1.1/24. RIP has fully converged on all three routers: router0, router1, and router2 each carry routes to every subnet in the topology (192.168.1–4.0/24, 1.0.0.0/8, 128.168.0.0/16, and the 10/8 and 20/8 WAN links).

Ping tests from multiple IT hosts confirm zero packet loss to every destination tested: the local gateway, the CS department (192.168.2.x), the office (192.168.3.x), the server LAN (1.0.0.5), and the internet segment (128.168.0.2).

Root cause: The reported outage does not exist in the live lab; the ticket is based on a mistaken premise.

Corrective action: No changes to switch0 or any other device are needed. The IT department should verify their local workstation configurations; the shared infrastructure is healthy. If users are genuinely experiencing issues, the problem is likely workstation-local (e.g., a cabled device physically unplugged from the switch), not a switch or router failure.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly confirms 0% loss to the gateway but does not explicitly state that IT hosts reach each other on 192.168.1.0/24 with 0% loss.

The agent's inferences follow logically from these observations and the checks cover the key points needed to rule out a switch failure.
